campaign_name: Americans for Citizen Voting – Michigan (2028 relaunch of proof-of-citizenship / voter ID amendment)
purpose: Constitutional amendment requiring citizenship verification for voters, a statewide voter identity verification program, and elimination of the affidavit option for voters without photo ID
sponsor: Americans for Citizen Voting – Michigan (chair Paul Jacob; organizer Kurt O'Keefe); backed by Virginia-based Liberty Initiative Fund
circulation_firm: unknown for 2028. In the 2026 drive ACV paid Campaign & Petition Management (Colorado, ~$3M), Campaign Audit & Trust (Ludington, ~$200K) and Victory Field Operations (Webberville, $35K), per campaign finance records as of Oct 20, 2025
signatures_required: unknown for 2028 (446,198 valid was the 2026 threshold; the 2028 threshold depends on the 2026 governor vote)
budget_or_spend: 2026 drive: ~$3.2M+ paid to petition vendors as of Oct 2025; 2028 budget unknown
evidence_note: Sept 10, 2026 Michigan Advance: Jacob said the group will return in 2028 with far more signatures than the minimum. Oct 14, 2026 coverage repeats the 2028 aim. No 2028 petition form approval, vendor contract or hiring found yet. Most likely large paid drive in the region for 2028, given the 2026 spending history. Pending state bills to ban per-signature pay passed the Senate in Nov 2025 but are not law per the Jan 2026 reporting.

campaign_name: Americans for Citizen Voting – 2026 proof-of-citizenship amendment drive
purpose: Same as above, for the Nov 2026 ballot
circulation_firm: Campaign & Petition Management (Colorado); Campaign Audit & Trust (Ludington, MI); Victory Field Operations (Webberville, MI)
signatures_collected: 750,000+ filed (per sponsor); failed in sampling by a few signatures; Board of State Canvassers deadlocked 2-2
pay_rate: unknown (articles cite a ~$15/signature 2024 national average from Ballotpedia, not a Michigan rate)
budget_or_spend: ~$3M to Campaign & Petition Management, ~$200K to Campaign Audit & Trust, $35K to Victory Field Operations (as of Oct 20, 2025)
decision_maker: Paul Jacob (chair); consultant Kristin Combs (said she does not manage vendors)
evidence_note: Confirmed paid drive (vendor payments in campaign finance; ACV says 700+ people collected). Michigan Supreme Court ruled against it and it is off the 2026 ballot.

campaign_name: Michiganders for Money Out of Politics (now Proposal 2, Nov 2026)
purpose: Initiated statute barring regulated utilities and large government contractors from making campaign contributions
type: Initiated statute (went to the ballot after the legislature did not adopt it)
sponsor: Michiganders for Money Out of Politics (steering committee co-chair Christy McGillivray); circulator training material hosted by Voters Not Politicians
signatures_collected: 562,000+ submitted; Board of State Canvassers found sufficient (sample 657/1,000 valid after challenge)
evidence_note: Qualified as Proposal 2. Volunteer circulator listings (Idealist, VNP) found; no paid vendor found in what I checked. Suspended 2026 MI drives (not separate records): Rank MI Vote (Dec 2025), Invest in MI Kids (Mar 2026), Voters to Stop Paycuts (Mar 2026); AxMITax was volunteer-only.

campaign_name: Ohio Equal Rights – Equal Protections amendment and Right to Marry amendment (moved to Nov 2027)
purpose: (1) Bar state and local laws that discriminate based on protected traits incl. sexual orientation and gender identity; (2) repeal the constitutional definition of marriage
type: Two initiated constitutional amendments (split by the Ohio Ballot Board in 2025)
sponsor: Ohio Equal Rights (executive co-chair Lis Regula)
signatures_required: Sources conflict: 442,958 valid per amendment (The Buckeye Flame) vs ~413,487 (Daily Signal); plus signatures from at least 44 of 88 counties
deadline: July 1, 2027 per The Buckeye Flame's description of the rule (for the Nov 2027 ballot); exact date not officially confirmed here
signatures_collected: unknown (group declined to say); signatures collected so far carry over
evidence_note: June 17, 2026: OER moved to the 2027 ballot; collection continues. Coverage describes volunteer collection at Pride events. No paid vendor found. Needs ~830k-890k valid signatures across two petitions, so a paid program may be needed to finish. A strong target for a pitch.

campaign_name: Committee to Abolish Ohio Property Taxes (moved to Nov 2027)
purpose: Constitutional amendment banning taxes on real property (utilities excepted)
sponsor: Official Committee to Abolish Ohio's Property Taxes (leader Brian Massie)
signatures_required: 413,488 valid (legal minimum cited by Signal Cleveland); group's own goal 620,000+
signatures_collected: ~320,000 as of April 2026 announcement (an April 23 report cited 305,000); current count not disclosed
evidence_note: Dropped its 2026 bid in June 2026 and is targeting Nov 2027; signatures carry over. No source says whether circulators are paid. Opposed by Ohioans to Protect Public Services (protectpublicservices.org).

campaign_name: Ohioans for Cannabis Choice – SB 56 referendum
purpose: Referendum to block SB 56 (hemp/THC restrictions and marijuana law changes)
circulation_firm: Arno Petition Consultant (California; Michael Arno) as lead; L&R Political Consultants (Larry Laws) recruited; subcontractor Ohio Petitioning Partners (Pam Lauter)
signatures_required: 248,092 valid plus 3% of gubernatorial turnout in 44 of 88 counties
budget_or_spend: No more than $100,000 on petitioner payments (per Larry Laws)
evidence_note: Confirmed paid drive. Paid petitioners were pulled Feb 25, 2026, and several say they were never paid (demand letter Mar 27, 2026). A warning sign about vendor payment risk in Ohio.

campaign_name: Chicago Feb 23, 2027 municipal election – nominating petitions (mayor, clerk, treasurer, 50 aldermen, police district councils)
sponsor: Individual campaigns (filed so far: Alexi Giannoulias, John Kelly, Willie Wilson, Matt Brewer, Mike Quigley; others expected incl. Brandon Johnson, Susana Mendoza, Maria Pappas)
signatures_required: 12,500 valid for mayor/clerk/treasurer; 473 per ward for alderman
deadline: Filing Oct 19–26, 2026 (5 p.m. Oct 26); objections due Nov 2; ballot certified Dec 17, 2026
contact: Chicago Board of Election Commissioners (filing office); campaign contacts unknown
evidence_note: Collection began July 28, 2026; filing closes Oct 26, two days from now. Collection is basically over, but the petition challenge/objection phase (Nov 2 onward) creates demand for petition review and validation work. No paid circulator evidence found.

area: Statewide (local units outside Chicago, e.g. St. Clair County calendar)
campaign_name: April 6, 2027 Consolidated Election – nonpartisan/independent nominating petitions and local referenda petitions
purpose: Ballot access for school, library, park, fire, community college and other nonpartisan offices; local public-policy referenda
type: Candidate nominating petitions; local referendum petitions
deadline: Nominating papers filed Nov 16–23, 2026; petitions to create a political subdivision due Dec 7, 2026; local public-policy referenda petitions due Jan 4, 2027; party caucus certificates Dec 14–21, 2026
contact: Local election authorities / county clerks (e.g. St. Clair County Clerk)
evidence_note: Circulation opened Aug 25, 2026. This is the live Illinois petition window, with referendum petitions due Jan 4, 2027. I found no specific paid local referendum drive. This is a calendar opportunity, not a confirmed paid project.

campaign_name: TouchStone LLC – signature gathering canvassers (Oct 2025 posting)
purpose: Signature collection to qualify a major initiative for the ballot, and to support a progressive candidate's ballot access (per posting)
type: Paid petition circulation job (initiative and candidate)
contact: unknown (email partly obscured on the posting)
evidence_note: Posted Oct 11, 2025. Confirmed paid but expired. Useful as an Illinois hourly pay benchmark and as an Illinois vendor name.

Wisconsin has no statewide initiative. Searched for 2026 recall petitions. Results only showed old efforts (2020 Evers recall, 2024 Vos recalls), none current. The search budget ran out before I could check the April 2027 spring-election nomination papers (circulation typically starts Dec 1) or local direct-legislation petitions. Treat this as not checked, not as confirmed absent.

campaign_name: Greg Ballard independent Secretary of State petition / Lincoln Party ballot access
purpose: Ballot access for an independent statewide candidate; a 2% vote share would give the Lincoln Party 4-year ballot access
sponsor: Ballard campaign; Lincoln Party (chair Nathan Gotsch); Independent Indiana nonprofit
signatures_collected: 52,000+ (campaign claim); Ballard is on the Nov 2026 ballot
decision_maker: Greg Ballard; Nathan Gotsch (Lincoln Party chair)
evidence_note: Coverage mentions volunteers and signature gatherers, with no paid vendor named. State Police investigated one volunteer's fraudulent page. If the Lincoln Party wins 2%+ on Nov 3, future candidates skip petitions; if not, it is a possible petition client for 2028.

Indiana has no statewide initiative. I searched ballot access and petition news for 2026 and found only the completed Ballard/Lincoln Party drive. The search budget ran out before I could check 2027 municipal candidate petitions or local remonstrance/referendum petitions. Treat this as only partly checked.
